metadata.title: Vortex transport and screening in a closed two-dimensional Bose field: friction, transverse force and diffusion of quantized vortices, and the polarisability of the thermal vortex-pair gas, measured in an energy-conserving classical field with no reservoir and no fit parameter (version 2, revised after peer review)
metadata.description:
Version 2.2 (October 2026): correction. The proportionality alpha ~ 0.24 rho_n/rho and its reading as a mode-averaged transport cross-section of 1.4 healing lengths hold at the single cutoff of this paper only; a scan of two further cutoffs (companion paper, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23262132) shows the friction follows the temperature, alpha ~ 0.054 T, independent of the cutoff, and withdraws the reading. A second correction: a second (Rust) implementation of the estimators shows that the energy estimator of alpha is biased low by diffusion (-8, -18, -22 % at eta = 5e-4, 1e-3, 2e-3 for a true alpha = 0.02), so the quoted alpha values are low by about 5-20 %; the regression estimator is unbiased. No registered verdict changes. Data and figures of the other sections are unchanged.

Version 2 (October 2026), revised after an external peer review (recorded verbatim in the repository, docs/peer_review/): physics narrative with the protocol moved to an appendix; seven figures (field maps of the old and corrected imprint, transport coefficients, residual mean-square displacement, stalled pairs with the parameter-free wind equation and the L = 96 control, phase portrait, charge structure factor, equilibration); explicit equations of the corrected imprint; the physics of the frame in which the transverse force is defined; a code appendix; and new results since version 1 -- the Josephson offset is not amplitude fluctuations (the phase-only correlator carries the same offset), vortices carry only a quarter of the normal density in the equilibrated L = 192 states, and the L = 96 counterflow control. The L = 96 counterflow control refutes the box mechanism (3 of 4 runs stall).

A quantized vortex in a thermal two-dimensional Bose gas is dragged by the normal fluid (friction α), possibly pushed sideways by it (transverse coefficient α′) and kicked by it (diffusion η). We measure the three coefficients in the projected Gross-Pitaevskii equation -- microcanonical, no damping term, no noise added -- with sub-grid vortex tracking and estimators that are identities of the dissipative point-vortex model, machine-checked in Lean 4. At T/T_BKT = 0.14, 0.27, 0.43: α = 0.0062(4), 0.014(2), 0.02(1), independent of pair size and estimator, α ≈ 0.24 ρ_n/ρ; α′ = 0 within 1 % once the kinematics of a compressible pair on a torus are accounted for (the Iordanskii value is excluded at 18σ); the vortex diffuses at 1.4-3 times the Einstein value, the relation itself undecided by the registered rule. A single pair in a closed box stops shrinking while the phonon band absorbs the impulse it sheds; the L = 96 control and a parameter-free wind equation are reported. The depressed stiffness of finite-box simulations is one unscreened box-scale pair that decays given time growing faster than L^2; the thermal pair gas has a k-independent charge structure factor equal to the Kosterlitz-Thouless polarisability from the measured pair sizes to 5-21 %, while a mode-by-mode dielectric relation fails. Every hypothesis, control and decision rule was committed before the data existed; failures are reported with the results.
metadata.notes: Version 2 after peer review 1. Registered verdicts unchanged from version 1 (friction criteria pass; Iordanskii-like prediction refuted; Einstein inconclusive by rule; equilibration E1/E3 pass, E2 fails on one run; dielectric D1/D2 fail, D4 passes). The L = 96 counterflow control (W2) (REFUTED) is reported with its registered binary reading and a parameter-free quantitative comparison. Companion software and data: concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22855581; Lean sources in the repository.
